transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I came in because when I start eating certain comfort foods, I can’t seem to stop. I’ll tell myself, “Maria, that’s enough,” but then my hand just goes right back to the pot anyway. It feels like I’m not in control of it.
Do you ever experience strong urges to engage in activities other than eating when you're stressed or emotional?
I don’t think so. Not that I’ve noticed, anyway. When I’m stressed or upset, it mostly just comes out around food. I can’t really think of another activity I get strong urges to do like that.
Does this loss of control happen only when you're eating, or are there other times when you feel like you're not in control?

It’s really just with eating. Once I start on those comfort foods, I’ll think, Maria, that’s enough, but then I still reach back for more, like I can’t make myself stop. I don’t feel that way with other things.
Is this loss of control limited to specific types of food, like the comfort foods you mentioned, or can it happen with any type of food?
It’s mostly those comfort foods, the ones I get started on and then I just keep going. I’ll tell myself, Maria, that’s enough, but my hand still goes back like I can’t quite make myself stop.
How often do these episodes of losing control while eating happen?
Since my friend passed, it’s been most weeks. Usually maybe once or twice a week, often in those quiet afternoons after choir or after I’ve been out gardening.
Do you usually feel guilty or ashamed after one of these episodes of eating comfort foods?
Yes… I do. Afterward I feel ashamed, and sad too. It feels like I took something that used to mean family and caring, and now it’s something I’m hiding from folks at church. That’s hard to sit with.
Would you say that when you have these episodes, you're eating a large amount of food?

Yes… I would say it’s a large amount. Like some afternoons after choir, or if I’ve been out in the garden, I’ll make myself a plate of rice and beans or chicken stew. Then I go back for more, and sometimes again, until I realize I’ve eaten enough for two or three meals.
When you're having one of these episodes with comfort foods, are you eating really quickly?
Yes… when it happens, I do eat fast. I’ve always been a slow eater, but lately I’ll be standing there by the counter, taking bite after bite, hardly even tasting it before the next one’s in my mouth.
Do you usually eat these comfort foods in response to a specific emotional state, like feeling sad or anxious?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed one clear feeling that starts it, like sadness or nerves every time. Sometimes I just find myself reaching for it, and then it keeps going.
Do you usually feel uncomfortably full after one of these episodes of eating comfort foods?
Yes. By the time I stop, my stomach feels tight and heavy. I usually have to sit down in my recliner and loosen my waistband because I’ve gone past what feels comfortable.
Do you feel like this eating behavior is interfering with your daily life or causing you a lot of distress?

It does bother me, yes. I still get to Mass and choir, and I keep up with my house, but after one of those afternoons I feel ashamed. Sometimes I just stay in and don’t call anybody because I’m embarrassed.
Do you feel like you're eating these comfort foods because you feel like you have to, or because you really want to?

It feels more like I have to, once I get started. I may want a little at first, but then I tell myself, “Maria, that’s enough,” and my hand still goes back to the pot. It’s like I can’t make myself stop.
Do you feel like you're eating these comfort foods as a way to escape or avoid thinking about your emotions or stress?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t thought of it that way. I know I reach for it when I’m sitting there and it’s around, but I don’t know if I’m trying to avoid my feelings exactly.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since these episodes of eating comfort foods started happening?
I’m not really sure. I don’t weigh myself much, and I haven’t noticed a big change in how my clothes fit. If there has been a change, I couldn’t say how much.
Have you ever tried to make up for eating a lot of comfort food by not eating much the next day or by exercising more?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really tried to make up for it like that. I might eat lighter just because I’m not as hungry, but I don’t set out to skip meals or exercise more because of it.
Have you ever hidden or thrown away food containers or evidence of your eating so that others wouldn't know how much you've eaten?
I don’t think so. I mean, I might throw wrappers or containers away like normal, but not really to hide how much I ate. I haven’t noticed myself trying to cover it up from anyone.
Have you ever made yourself vomit after one of these episodes of eating comfort foods?
No, I haven’t done that. I’ve never made myself throw up after eating like that.
Do you often criticize yourself after one of these episodes of eating comfort foods?

Yes… I do. Afterward I feel ashamed and sad. It feels like I took something that used to mean family and caring, you know, comfort food, and turned it into something I feel like I have to hide from people at church.
